_real_world.class: AESA fire-control radar, type not officially disclosed
_real_world.variant_scope: J-35 carrier-based stealth fighter nose radar; several public sources suggest kinship with the J-20's Type 1475 AESA, unconfirmed
public_equipment: AESA radar (OOB page, C-tier, 'type not public'); one blog source names 'Type 1475 AESA (same as J-20)' with a claimed 1,500 km detection range against unspecified target class, unverified

_provenance.modeling_note: Primary fire-control radar for the carrier-based J-35 per the task's requirement. No official PRC disclosure of the J-35's radar type or performance exists; the OOB page itself states 'Radar: AESA; type not public' at C-tier only, and the export FC-31's advertised KLJ-7A radar is explicitly noted as not applicable to the naval J-35. A single blog-tier source (not independently corroborated, not in the ledger) claims a 'Type 1475 AESA (same as J-20)' fit with a 1,500 km detection figure; that 1,500 km number is almost certainly a garbled/exaggerated derivative-target claim (implausible for any fighter radar against a fighter-size target) and is explicitly rejected here as unusable. max_range is therefore an engineering_estimate proxy set modestly above the repo CSG_US_APG-79 (150 km, Super Hornet AESA) to reflect the general public expectation that a newer-generation Chinese naval AESA (contemporary with J-20-era radars) should be at least competitive with a 2010s-vintage Western AESA, while avoiding any reliance on the unverifiable 1,500 km claim. All other scan/track/noise parameters are proxies patterned on the repo CSG_US_APG-79 record, nudged slightly toward its own AESA-vs-mechanically-scanned-array reasoning; no public figures exist for any of them.

sensor.max_range.note: engineering_estimate 170 km, modestly above the repo CSG_US_APG-79's 150 km sourced figure, reflecting general expectation of a newer-generation AESA; the only web-found specific figure (1,500 km, blog-tier, unverified) is explicitly rejected as implausible for a fighter fire-control radar against a fighter-size target and not used
